boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Hawaii at Manoa, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure sequence for learning the campus, finding student resources, and making a few under-21-safe plans.

cards.title: Start with the campus map
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · learn the landmarks
cards.notes: Open the official map before heading out, then pin a few destinations you expect to revisit: Campus Center, Hamilton Library, recreation, and your next class building.
cards.short_summary: Build a practical mental map before wandering farther.
cards.evidence_claim: UH Mānoa’s Campus Maps page provides map layers for campus buildings, dining, transportation, parking, and health and wellness locations.
cards.access_notes: Use the official map’s current layers and destination details; campus access and building hours can vary.

cards.title: Make Campus Center your first hub
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · 2465 Campus Road
cards.notes: Walk through the student union to locate the information office, bookstore, meeting areas, and dining options. It is a useful reset point between other campus stops.
cards.short_summary: Get oriented at the campus’s central student hub.
cards.evidence_claim: UH Mānoa identifies Campus Center as the primary location for meetings, dining, entertainment, and campus events for the Mānoa community.
cards.access_notes: Campus Center facilities and individual services may have separate operating hours.

cards.title: Pause for a campus meal
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Campus Center, second floor
cards.notes: Use a meal or snack break to get comfortable in the building. Check the dining page on the day you go, since service hours and vendors can change by term.
cards.short_summary: Pair orientation with a straightforward food stop.
cards.evidence_claim: The Campus Center Food Court is located on the second floor of Campus Center at 2465 Campus Road and accepts meal plans, Dining Dollars, and Bonus Dollars.
cards.access_notes: Purchase required for food; consult the official dining page for current hours and closures.

cards.title: Find your library base
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Maile Way
cards.notes: Take a first lap through Hamilton, locate a seat that suits you, and save the library hours page. It can also help you plan a quieter return visit.
cards.short_summary: Choose a reliable study and research anchor early.
cards.evidence_claim: Hamilton Library is UH Mānoa’s largest building and the state’s largest research library; the library publishes its building hours online.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces – Student Academic Success Center
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current online hours before visiting, especially on weekends and holidays.

cards.title: Check out the Warrior Rec Center
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Campus Center
cards.notes: Bring your current UH ID and review entry rules before going. A short visit can help you decide whether the track, fitness areas, or a class fits your routine.
cards.short_summary: Get acquainted with an on-campus recreation option.
cards.evidence_claim: UH Mānoa describes the Warrior Recreation Center as a multi-level gym at Campus Center with an indoor track, classes, and weight-training space.
cards.source_title: Student Co-Curricular Success – Departments and Programs
cards.access_notes: General facility hours and entry requirements are published by Student Recreation Services; access depends on membership eligibility and rules.

cards.title: Take a garden walk
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · behind Jefferson Hall
cards.notes: Use the garden as a calm outdoor waypoint while learning the east side of campus. Stay on established paths and treat the tea house and garden features respectfully.
cards.short_summary: Add a quiet cultural landscape to your campus walk.
cards.evidence_claim: UH news describes the East-West Center Japanese Garden as the setting of the traditional tea house, with trees and a koi pond.
cards.source_title: Traditional Japanese tea house marks 50 years at UH Mānoa
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor garden area; respect posted notices and any event or facility restrictions.

cards.title: See what is showing at the Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Art Building, 2535 McCarthy Mall
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition and gallery calendar, then make time for a short, unhurried visit. It is an easy way to see campus creative work without leaving Mānoa.
cards.short_summary: Work a current exhibition into your campus exploration.
cards.evidence_claim: The UH Art Gallery is on the first floor of the Art Building at 2535 McCarthy Mall; the university catalog states that admission is free.
cards.access_notes: The catalog lists Tuesday–Friday and Sunday gallery hours; confirm the current exhibition schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Plan an open-swim visit
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening · Lower Campus
cards.notes: If swimming is your thing, review the official open-swim schedule and facility rules before you go. Keep this as an optional active stop rather than a fixed commitment.
cards.short_summary: Use the published schedule to test an on-campus swim session.
cards.evidence_claim: Student Recreation Services publishes open-swim hours for the Duke Kahanamoku Aquatic Complex as part of its recreation facility schedule.
cards.source_title: Recreation Facilities Hours – Student Life & Development
cards.access_notes: Open-swim times are term-specific and facilities may close during breaks, holidays, emergencies, or staff training; verify before leaving.

cards.title: Check the Kennedy Theatre calendar
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening · 1770 East-West Road
cards.notes: Browse the season before committing to a ticket, then choose a performance that fits your weekend. Bring a current UH Mānoa ID if you use a student ticket offer.
cards.short_summary: Keep a campus performance on your radar for a future night out.
cards.evidence_claim: Kennedy Theatre is the home base for UH Mānoa Department of Theatre & Dance productions, and validated UH Mānoa students can buy regular-season tickets at the listed student price.
cards.source_title: Ticketing Information – John F. Kennedy Theatre
cards.access_notes: Ticket availability, show dates, and prices vary by production; review the official calendar and ticketing page before attending.

cards.title: End by browsing student organizations
cards.subtitle: Sunday · choose one interest to follow up
cards.notes: Look for a group aligned with an interest you already have, then note its next meeting or contact. One small follow-up is enough for a first weekend.
cards.short_summary: Turn a campus walk into one potential connection.
cards.evidence_claim: UH Mānoa encourages students to participate in nearly 200 Registered Independent Organizations and chartered student organizations.
cards.source_title: Students – University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa
cards.access_notes: Organization membership, meeting times, and eligibility differ by group; contact the organization or Student Life & Development for current details.
